item.content:encoded:
Eligibility

  • Bachelor’s/Master’s degree graduates with distinction or higher (CPA of 3.2 or above).
  • Proficiency in English (equivalent to IELTS 6.0 or above).
  • Passion for scientific research.
  • Prior experience in research projects and published papers is an advantage (but not mandatory).

 

Scholarship Programs

1. 89-Topup Scholarship

  • Designed for faculty members from universities.
  • Applicants will receive guidance on applying for the 89 Scholarship from the Ministry of Education, selecting UTS as their host university.
  • Upon receiving the 89 Scholarship, applicants will also receive a UTS top-up scholarship worth AUD 38,000/year and an additional AUD 5,000 start-up grant.

2. JRC Scholarship

  • For those ineligible for the Ministry of Education’s 89 Scholarship.
  • Recipients of the JRC Scholarship will study 1-2 years at HUST and at least 1 year at UTS.
  • While at HUST, they will receive funding from AI4LIFE Institute’s budget.
  • During their time at UTS, they will receive a full scholarship funded by UTS.

 

Selection Process

Round 1: Application Submission

  • Copy of Bachelor’s/Master’s degree (for Master’s graduates).
  • Academic transcripts from the most recent degree level.
  • Recommendation letters (at least two).
  • Acceptance letters from supervisors (one from HUST, one from UTS) (optional).

Submission link

Round 2: Interview

  • Presentation of research content and proposal.
  • Q&A with the selection committee.

 

Supervisors

  1. Supervisors at UTS: List 
  2. Supervisors at HUST

    • All faculty members at HUST (meeting HUST’s requirements for PhD supervision) are eligible to supervise candidates under this program.

    • Applicants may also refer to faculty members currently conducting research at AI4LIFE (here).
